## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Limited information is available about the wave sizes this break works in.
- Limited information is available about this break's preferred tide conditions.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Four publishers: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surf Atlas and Stormrider (region page). Wind: SE offshore (Surf-Forecast, 25 deg from the profile's 110) and a SE-E-NE window (WannaSurf) both agree; no source names a single easterly offshore exactly. Swell direction: NNW (Surf-Forecast), N-NW (Surf Atlas) and NW-W-SW (WannaSurf) all overlap the profile's 300-330 optimum; the evidence leans more northerly than the profile, and WannaSurf's SW is outside the window. Size: only WannaSurf (5 to 16 ft or more), consistent with the profile's 4-15 ft. Tide: WannaSurf low to mid (overlaps the profile's mid); Stormrider warns that some Ericeira ledges get dangerous at low tide (region-wide, not recorded). Season: Surf Atlas November-March for the northern reefs; Stormrider says autumn for Ericeira as a whole; Surf-Forecast says it can work any time of year. Gaps: no swell period figure from any source; no peer-reviewed or official source on Coxos. Crossref found two Ericeira World Surfing Reserve wave-modelling papers (ICCE 2025, OMAE 2024); the readable ICCE extended abstract does not mention Coxos, so nothing was recorded.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 5–6 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | — | not documented | — | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 16 ft | documented | S2 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.5-2 m / 5-6 ft (the page's own conversion; face or offshore height not stated); it is the only size source.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
- **Ideal range**: No excerpt states an ideal or best size range.
- **Maximum suitable**: WannaSurf says it holds up to 5 m / 16 ft and over, an open-ended bound (scale not stated); it is the only size source.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal bearing | 337.5° (NNW) | documented | S1 | `optimal_swell_direction` 300–330° (WNW to NNW, clockwise) |
| Acceptable range | 225–360° (SW to N, clockwise) | documented | S2, S3 | `swell_window` 260–350° (W to N, clockwise) |

| Exposure | exposed reef break with fairly consistent surf that can work at any time of year | documented | S1 | no setting |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives north-northwest as the best swell direction; NNW = 337.5 deg.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “the best swell direction is from the north northwest”
- **Acceptable range**: WannaSurf lists NW, W and SW as good directions (225-315 deg) and Surf Atlas says north and north-west swells push power into Coxos (315-360 deg); the value spans both, which share NW.
  - S2 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionNorthWest, West, SouthWest”
  - S3 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “The north and north-west swells can fire on all cylinders at this time of year, pushing power straight into Coxos and its neighbours.”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names swell directions that are blocked or shadowed by land or reefs.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls Coxos an exposed reef break with fairly consistent surf that can work at any time of the year.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Coxos in Ericeira is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf and can work at any time of the year.”

Notes:

  - S3 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “Winter (November-March)...This is when the famous reefs that string along the headlands to the north of the town really come into their own.”
  - S4 (Stormrider Surf Guides): “Autumn (Sep–Nov) brings the most reliable surf with favourable winds and solid swells”
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Coxos in Ericeira is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf and can work at any time of the year.”
- **Secondary season**: No excerpt states a secondary or shoulder season.
- **Swell sources**: Surf Atlas says the north and north-west swells fire in winter, pushing power straight into Coxos.
  - S3 (Surf Atlas (thesurfatlas.com)): “The north and north-west swells can fire on all cylinders at this time of year, pushing power straight into Coxos and its neighbours.”
- **Wind patterns**: Stormrider says autumn brings the most reliable surf with favourable winds and solid swells, for Ericeira as a whole; it names no direction.
  - S4 (Stormrider Surf Guides): “Autumn (Sep–Nov) brings the most reliable surf with favourable winds and solid swells”

## Conflicting information

- **Seasonality · prime months**: Surf Atlas says the northern reefs, Coxos among them, come into their own in winter (November-March), while Stormrider says autumn (September-November) brings Ericeira's most reliable surf (region-wide), and Surf-Forecast says it can work at any time of year; only November is common to the two month ranges.
